name: @psyb0t/stealthy-auto-browse
summary: Wire an OpenClaw agent to a self-hosted stealthy-auto-browse stealth browser over MCP — navigation, OS-level input, screenshots, and page inspection as tools.
description: A thin stdio<->HTTP bridge that connects an MCP client (OpenClaw, Claude, Cursor, Codex, ...) to a running stealthy-auto-browse instance's MCP endpoint (/mcp), exposing its browser-automation tools: navigation, Playwright DOM input (click/fill), OS-level input via PyAutoGUI (system_click/system_type/send_key/mouse_move/scroll), screenshots, page inspection (get_text/get_html/get_interactive_elements/eval_js), wait conditions, multi-step scripts (run_script), and a generic browser_action fallback for cookies/tabs/storage/dialogs/recording. stealthy-auto-browse is self-hosted — you run the container yourself and point this bridge at it. These tools drive a real browser and OS-level keyboard/mouse input on the machine running the server and can log into sites and act as you — use it ONLY against systems and sites you are authorized to control, and only for actions the user explicitly requested. See https://github.com/psyb0t/docker-stealthy-auto-browse.

STEALTHY_AUTO_BROWSE_URL.description: Base URL of your running stealthy-auto-browse server, e.g. http://localhost:8080 (the bridge appends /mcp).

AUTH_TOKEN.description: Bearer token, only if the stealthy-auto-browse server was started with AUTH_TOKEN set.
